Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/17588b058b1e1fe934e06679836234f0ef35fe4484a558fcc3ec3b2aafbd2620.png) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol f$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol f$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/613ba027e9564812a8e050efd69fd98fff3f614f7d2ec69eeb787c628ccabd12.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y)=2xy, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y)={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

e-12478.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/f1c18d26fb7b6f1969bcda14d71ac18429466b4be8847097f227cdc537fdc8d9.png) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/4b752e33d4ca3154590a5dc16ec3addd1d45a9618c92283903ff33d3818b8266.png)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/d10e552c42ff8fe0df517b6297582bd5eeefdf29896a51005c79bd399a363c13.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2})=2y, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\frac{y}{x},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y\operatorname{ln}⁡x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/8c2cef2ba5322cc545860caa4d2f503f5f48a3374cce7c0f1e910a56f0357a64.png)
Thus, the missing entries are $y,\:$ $0,\:$ and $\ln{x}.$

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})=3{x}^{2},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{e}^{y})={e}^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/a8fd9120b29337c656c9b715bfa38dbecc7755e50877fad9719de54ed248a8ed.png)

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/445be7536a39ee9c8d90f4cee571bf46acb5c995a9b53547f1aa582bd351592a.png) we have

The tangent to $f$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
z - f(\mathbf a) = \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $f(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

what are the missing values?
e-12484.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $\boldsymbol{f}:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m$ is defined by 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/eb248ccd80e8a10edab9d44c4cb11841aad35f6d35a778ff828607a312fcad35.png) 

where $f_1,f_2,\ldots,f_m$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $\boldsymbol{f}$ is differentiable at $\mathbf{x},$ then the total derivative of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf{x},$ denoted $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf{x}),$ is given by the $m \times n$ matrix

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/47d512d278eaa912a112e96406e44d8b9a464984487e0ab9ff253a233441c2e1.png)

In our case, we have the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/4bb0fb226d008d5efe2e7a04a444a2313b2acf80f71589a2aa0a17e40246c03b.png)

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})={x}_{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{1},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1})=\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{1} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=0,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡{x}_{2})=\operatorname{cos}⁡{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/9eb84e24979469e9b1618f0a20f030963741a513292699ed4c4d342cd9d8e00d.png)

Evaluating $\boldsymbol{f}$ and its derivative at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094602/assets/22f4d34b8ec830740b285e1c31954b1e382264c4f366d3ea426ecadd3fd5f5bb.png) we have

The linear approximation of $\boldsymbol{f}$ at $\mathbf x = \mathbf a$ is given by

$$
\boldsymbol{f}\left(\mathbf x \right) \approx \boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a) + \boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a)(\mathbf x - \mathbf a).
$$

Substituting $\boldsymbol{f}(\mathbf a),$ $\boldsymbol{f}'(\mathbf a),$ and $\mathbf a$ in the equation above, we obtain

after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1)} & -\frac{(-2)}{(1)^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}].

EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(xy)=1y,∂f∂y=∂∂y(xy)=−xy2

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[1y−xy2]

and f′ at a=[−21] is

f′(a)=[1(1)−(−2)(1)2]=[12].

$$
f(x)=\frac{x}{y},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{y})=\frac{1}{y}, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{y})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{y} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

and ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(1)} & -\frac{(-2)}{(1)^{2}}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

f(x)=x2−xy+y2,x=[xy],

calculate f′(x).

a
[2x−12y−1]
b
[2y−x2x−y]
c
[2x−12y−1]
d
[2y−x−y+2x]
e
[2x−y−x+2y]
Submit

decision.explanation: The partial derivatives are ∂f/∂x=2x−y and ∂f/∂y=−x+2y. The derivative is their row matrix, matching option e.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
For the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2})=2x-y, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2})=-x+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x-y & -x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2})=2x-y, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-xy+{y}^{2})=-x+2y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2x-y & -x+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+3{y}^{2})=3{x}^{2}, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+3{y}^{2})=6y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & 6y\end{aligned}]
$$

and ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2} & 6(-1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 3
?

For the transformation f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=x3+3y2,x=[xy],

calculate f′ at a=[1−1].

a
[63]
b
[36]
c
[−36]
d
[3−6]
e
[3−6−63]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(x3+3y2)=3x2,∂f∂y=∂∂y(x3+3y2)=6y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[3x26y]

and f′ at a=[1−1] is

f′(a)=[3(1)26(−1)]=[3−6].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Scalar Function
content.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)={x}^{3}+3{y}^{2},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+3{y}^{2})=3{x}^{2}, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+3{y}^{2})=6y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2} & 6y\end{aligned}]
$$

and ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2} & 6(-1)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(2x2−3y2)=4x,∂f∂y=∂∂y(2x2−3y2)=−6y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[4x−6y].

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=x{y}^{2}-y,\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-y)={y}^{2}, & \,\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-y)=2xy-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & 2xy-1\end{aligned}]
$$

and ${f}^{′}$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]$ is

$$
{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}(1)^{2} & 2(0)(1)-1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(xy2−y)=y2,∂f∂y=∂∂y(xy2−y)=2xy−1

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[y22xy−1]

and f′ at a=[0−1] is

f′(a)=[(1)22(0)(1)−1]=[1−1].

f(x)=[\begin{aligned}2xy \\ {e}^{xy}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],

decision.explanation: The Jacobian has one row per output component. Differentiating 2xy gives [2y,2x]; differentiating e^(xy) gives [ye^(xy),xe^(xy)] by the chain rule. These rows form option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}2xy \\ {e}^{xy}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy)=2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy)=2x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy})=y{e}^{xy},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy})=x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2y & 2x \\ y{e}^{xy} & x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 6
?

For the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[2xyexy],x=[xy],

calculate f′(x).

a
[yexy2x2yxexy]
b
[2xxexy]
c
[2yyexy]
d
[2y2xyexyxexy]
e
[2xy2xyexyexy]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f2∂x∂f2∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(2xy)=2y,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(2xy)=2x∂f2∂x=∂∂x(exy)=yexy,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(exy)=xexy

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[2y2xyexyxexy].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Vector Function
content.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}2xy \\ {e}^{xy}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy)=2y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy)=2x \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xy})=y{e}^{xy},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xy})=x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}2y & 2x \\ y{e}^{xy} & x{e}^{xy}\end{aligned}].
$$

before.problem:

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{xyz} \\ x+yz\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],

Question 7
?

For the transformation f:R3→R2, defined as

f(x)=[exyzx+yz],x=[xyz],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[AAxzexyzxyexyz1AAAA]. From left to right, what are the missing entries?

a
zexyz, z, and z
b
xexyz, z, and z
c
exyz, 2x, and y
d
yzeyz, 0, and y
e
yzexyz, z, and y
Submit

decision.explanation: The missing entries are ∂(e^(xyz))/∂x=yz e^(xyz), ∂(x+yz)/∂y=z, and ∂(x+yz)/∂z=y. These match option e.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{xyz} \\ x+yz\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned} & xz{e}^{xyz} & xy{e}^{xyz} \\ 1 &  & \end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xyz})=yz{e}^{xyz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xyz})=xz{e}^{xyz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{xyz})=xy{e}^{xyz} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+yz)=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+yz)=z,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+yz)=y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}yz{e}^{xyz} & xz{e}^{xyz} & xy{e}^{xyz} \\ 1 & z & y\end{aligned}].
$$

after.html:
Question 7
?

For the transformation f:R3→R2, defined as

f(x)=[exyzx+yz],x=[xyz],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[AAxzexyzxyexyz1AAAA]. From left to right, what are the missing entries?

a
zexyz, z, and z
b
xexyz, z, and z
c
exyz, 2x, and y
d
yzeyz, 0, and y
e
yzexyz, z, and y
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f1∂z∂f2∂x∂f2∂y∂f2∂z]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(exyz)=yzexyz,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(exyz)=xzexyz,∂f1∂z=∂∂z(exyz)=xyexyz∂f2∂x=∂∂x(x+yz)=1,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(x+yz)=z,∂f2∂z=∂∂z(x+yz)=y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[yzexyzxzexyzxyexyz1zy].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution gives the missing entries as yz e^(xyz), z, and y, exactly option e. This agrees with differentiating e^(xyz) with respect to x and x+yz with respect to y and z.

content.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{xyz} \\ x+yz\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned} & xz{e}^{xyz} & xy{e}^{xyz} \\ 1 &  & \end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{xyz})=yz{e}^{xyz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{xyz})=xz{e}^{xyz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({e}^{xyz})=xy{e}^{xyz} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x+yz)=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x+yz)=z,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+yz)=y\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}yz{e}^{xyz} & xz{e}^{xyz} & xy{e}^{xyz} \\ 1 & z & y\end{aligned}].
$$

before.html:
Question 8
?

For the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[x−yex−y],x=[xy],

calculate f′(x).

a
[1−1ex−yex−y]
b
[1−1ex−y−ex−y]
c
[1−ex−yex+y−1]
d
[1−1ex−e−y]
e
[11−ex−y−ex−y]
Submit

decision.explanation: The Jacobian rows are [1,−1] for x−y and [e^(x−y),−e^(x−y)] for e^(x−y), using the chain rule. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}x-y \\ {e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-y)=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-y)=-1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x-y})={e}^{x-y},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x-y})=-{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ {e}^{x-y} & -{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 8
?

For the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[x−yex−y],x=[xy],

calculate f′(x).

a
[1−1ex−yex−y]
b
[1−1ex−y−ex−y]
c
[1−ex−yex+y−1]
d
[1−1ex−e−y]
e
[11−ex−y−ex−y]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f2∂x∂f2∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(x−y)=1,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(x−y)=−1∂f2∂x=∂∂x(ex−y)=ex−y,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(ex−y)=−ex−y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[1−1ex−y−ex−y].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Vector Function
content.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}x-y \\ {e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

calculate ${f}^{′}(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x-y)=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x-y)=-1 \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({e}^{x-y})={e}^{x-y},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({e}^{x-y})=-{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ {e}^{x-y} & -{e}^{x-y}\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 9
?

For the transformation f:R2→R3, defined as

f(x)=[xyx2−ysin⁡(xy)],x=[xy],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[yAAAA−1AAxcos⁡(xy)]. From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?

a
x, 2x, and xsin⁡(xy)
b
x, 2x, and ycos⁡(xy)
c
x, 2x, and ysin⁡(xy)
d
x, x, and xcos⁡(xy)
e
x, x, and ycos⁡(xy)
Submit

decision.explanation: From top to bottom, the missing entries are ∂(xy)/∂y=x, ∂(x²−y)/∂x=2x, and ∂sin(xy)/∂x=y cos(xy), matching option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}xy \\ {x}^{2}-y \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y &  \\  & -1 \\  & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].
$$

From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-y)=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-y)=-1, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 2x & -1 \\ y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy) & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, the missing entries are $x,\,$ $2x,\,$ and $y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).$

Question 9

For the transformation f:R2→R3, defined as

f(x)=[xyx2−ysin⁡(xy)],x=[xy],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[yAAAA−1AAxcos⁡(xy)]. From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?

a
x, 2x, and xsin⁡(xy)
b
x, 2x, and ycos⁡(xy)
c
x, 2x, and ysin⁡(xy)
d
x, x, and xcos⁡(xy)
e
x, x, and ycos⁡(xy)
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f2∂x∂f2∂y∂f3∂x∂f3∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(xy)=y,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(xy)=x,∂f2∂x=∂∂x(x2−y)=2x,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(x2−y)=−1,∂f3∂x=∂∂x(sin⁡(xy))=ycos⁡(xy),∂f3∂y=∂∂y(sin⁡(xy))=xcos⁡(xy)

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[yx2x−1ycos⁡(xy)xcos⁡(xy)].

Thus, the missing entries are x, 2x, and ycos⁡(xy).

verification.explanation: The revealed solution explicitly gives x, 2x, and y cos(xy), matching option b. Independent differentiation agrees: ∂(xy)/∂y=x, ∂(x²−y)/∂x=2x, and ∂sin(xy)/∂x=y cos(xy).

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Derivative of a Vector Function
content.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}xy \\ {x}^{2}-y \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y &  \\  & -1 \\  & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].
$$

From top to bottom, what are the missing entries?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy)=y,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy)=x, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}-y)=2x,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}-y)=-1, \\ \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{3}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy))=x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}y & x \\ 2x & -1 \\ y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy) & x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}].
$$

Thus, the missing entries are $x,\,$ $2x,\,$ and $y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy).$

before.html:
Question 10
?

For the transformation f:R3→R2, defined as

f(x)=[xyzx2yz2],x=[xyz],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[AA−xy2zAA2xyz2AA2x2yz]. From left to right, what are the missing entries?

a
 1yz, x2yz2, and xyz2
b
1z, xz, and −xyz
c
−1yz, x2yz2, and −xyz2
d
−xy2z2, x2+z2, and −xyz
e
1yz, x2z2, and −xyz2
Submit

decision.explanation: Reading the blanks from left to right gives ∂(x/(yz))/∂x=1/(yz), ∂(x²yz²)/∂y=x²z², and ∂(x/(yz))/∂z=−x/(yz²). These match option e, on the domain yz≠0.

after.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{yz} \\ {x}^{2}y{z}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z} &  \\ 2xy{z}^{2} &  & 2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{yz})=\frac{1}{yz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{yz})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{x}{yz})=-\frac{x}{y{z}^{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})=2xy{z}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})={x}^{2}{z}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})=2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{yz} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z} & -\frac{x}{y{z}^{2}} \\ 2xy{z}^{2} & {x}^{2}{z}^{2} & 2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 10

For the transformation f:R3→R2, defined as

f(x)=[xyzx2yz2],x=[xyz],

the total derivative f′ is given by

f′(x)=[AA−xy2zAA2xyz2AA2x2yz]. From left to right, what are the missing entries?

a
 1yz, x2yz2, and xyz2
b
1z, xz, and −xyz
c
−1yz, x2yz2, and −xyz2
d
−xy2z2, x2+z2, and −xyz
e
1yz, x2z2, and −xyz2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x∂f1∂y∂f1∂z∂f2∂x∂f2∂y∂f2∂z]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x=∂∂x(xyz)=1yz,∂f1∂y=∂∂y(xyz)=−xy2z,∂f1∂z=∂∂z(xyz)=−xyz2∂f2∂x=∂∂x(x2yz2)=2xyz2,∂f2∂y=∂∂y(x2yz2)=x2z2,∂f2∂z=∂∂z(x2yz2)=2x2yz

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[1yz−xy2z−xyz22xyz2x2z22x2yz].

content.problem:
For the transformation $f:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{yz} \\ {x}^{2}y{z}^{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}],
$$

the total derivative ${f}^{′}$ is given by 

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z} &  \\ 2xy{z}^{2} &  & 2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}].
$$

From left to right, what are the missing entries?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{yz})=\frac{1}{yz},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{yz})=-\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{x}{yz})=-\frac{x}{y{z}^{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})=2xy{z}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})={x}^{2}{z}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}y{z}^{2})=2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{yz} & -\frac{x}{{y}^{2}z} & -\frac{x}{y{z}^{2}} \\ 2xy{z}^{2} & {x}^{2}{z}^{2} & 2{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{xy+1},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
after.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{xy+1})=-\frac{y}{(xy+1)^{2}},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{xy+1})=-\frac{x}{(xy+1)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{(xy+1)^{2}} & -\frac{x}{(xy+1)^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=\frac{1}{2},\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-\frac{1}{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{1}{4})+(-\frac{1}{4})=0.
$$

Question 11

Consider the function f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=1xy+1,x=[xy].

If the tangent to f at a=[11] is given by

z−∗=[∗∗]([xy]−[11])

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
1
b
−14
c
0
d
12
e
14
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(1xy+1)=−y(xy+1)2,∂f∂y=∂∂y(1xy+1)=−x(xy+1)2

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[−y(xy+1)2−x(xy+1)2].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[11], we have

f(a)=12,f′(a)=[−14−14].

The tangent to f at x=a is given by

z−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

z−12=[−14−14]([xy]−[11]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

12+(−14)+(−14)=0.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution declares the sum to be 1/2−1/4−1/4=0, exactly option c. Independent evaluation of f and its partial derivatives at (1,1) agrees.

content.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{xy+1},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{xy+1})=-\frac{y}{(xy+1)^{2}},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{xy+1})=-\frac{x}{(xy+1)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{y}{(xy+1)^{2}} & -\frac{x}{(xy+1)^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=\frac{1}{2},\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-\frac{1}{2}=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} & -\frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{1}{4})+(-\frac{1}{4})=0.
$$

after.html:
Question 12
?

Consider the function f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=yx2+1,x=[xy].

If the tangent to f at a=[−10] is given by

z−∗=[∗∗]([xy]−[−10])

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
−1
b
12
c
−12
d
1
e
0
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(yx2+1)=−2xy(x2+1)2,∂f∂y=∂∂y(yx2+1)=1x2+1

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[−2xy(x2+1)21x2+1].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[−10], we have

f(a)=0,f′(a)=[012].

The tangent to f at x=a is given by

z−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

z−0=[012]([xy]−[−10]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

0+0+12=12.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangent Plane to the Graph of a Scalar Function in Matrix Form
content.problem:
Consider the function $f:{R}^{2}\to R,$ defined as

$$
f(x)=\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+1},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].
$$

If the tangent to $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
z-∗=[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}])
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+1})=-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+1)^{2}},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+1})=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+1)^{2}} & \frac{1}{{x}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=0,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-0=[\begin{aligned}0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
0+0+\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

f(x)=\frac{{e}^{2x}}{y},\,x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}].

$$

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{y})=\frac{2{e}^{2x}}{y},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{y})=-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2{e}^{2x}}{y} & -\frac{{e}^{2x}}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

$$

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(e2xy)=2e2xy,∂f∂y=∂∂y(e2xy)=−e2xy2

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[2e2xy−e2xy2].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[12], we have

f(a)=e22,f′(a)=[e2−e24].

The tangent to f at x=a is given by

z−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

z−e22=[e2−e24]([xy]−[12]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

e22+e2+(−e24)=5e24.

content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{y})=\frac{2{e}^{2x}}{y},\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{e}^{2x}}{y})=-\frac{{e}^{2x}}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2{e}^{2x}}{y} & -\frac{{e}^{2x}}{{y}^{2}}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=\frac{{e}^{2}}{2},\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & -\frac{{e}^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2} & -\frac{{e}^{2}}{4}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}+{e}^{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{2}}{4})=\frac{5{e}^{2}}{4}.
$$

Question 15

Consider the function f:R2→R, defined as

f(x)=x3ln⁡y,x=[xy].

If the tangent to f at a=[1e] is given by

z−∗=[∗∗]([xy]−[1e])

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
5e+2e
b
3e+4e
c
4e−1e
d
4e+1e
e
3e−2e
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f∂x∂f∂y]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f∂x=∂∂x(x3ln⁡y)=3x2ln⁡y,∂f∂y=∂∂y(x3ln⁡y)=x3y

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[3x2ln⁡yx3y].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[1e], we have

f(a)=1,f′(a)=[31e].

The tangent to f at x=a is given by

z−f(a)=f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

z−1=[31e]([xy]−[1e]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

1+3+1e=4e+1e.

Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & \frac{∂f}{∂y}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y,\, & \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡y)=\frac{{x}^{3}}{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & \frac{{x}^{3}}{y}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ e\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=1,\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}3 & \frac{1}{e}\end{aligned}].
$$

The tangent to $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
z-f(a)={f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
z-1=[\begin{aligned}3 & \frac{1}{e}\end{aligned}]([\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ e\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
1+3+\frac{1}{e}=\frac{4e+1}{e}.
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?

b

EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(x13−x2)=3x12,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(x13−x2)=−1∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(x2ex1)=x2ex1,∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(x2ex1)=ex1

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[3x12−1x2ex1ex1].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[0−1], we have

f(a)=[1−1],f′(a)=[0−1−11].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[1−1]+[0−1−11](x−[0−1]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

1+(−1)+1=1.

Question 17
?

Consider the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[x2ex13x1+2x2],x=[x1x2].

If the linear approximation of f at a=[01] is given by

f(x)≈[∗2]+[1∗∗2](x−[01]),

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
3
b
5
c
7
d
2
e
1
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(x2ex1)=x2ex1,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(x2ex1)=ex1∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(3x1+2x2)=3,∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(3x1+2x2)=2

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[x2ex1ex132].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[01], we have

f(a)=[12],f′(a)=[1132].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[12]+[1132](x−[01]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

1+1+3=5.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution states that the missing values are 1, 1, and 3, whose sum is 5. This matches option b and agrees with independent evaluation of f and its Jacobian at (0,1).

content.knowledge_point: Finding an Affine Approximation of a Vector Function
content.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}} \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at  $a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & ∗ \\ ∗ & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}})={x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}})={e}^{{x}_{1}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2})=3,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2})=2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{2}{e}^{{x}_{1}} & {e}^{{x}_{1}} \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
1+1+3=5.
$$

Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1})=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1})=-{x}_{2}^{-2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -{x}_{2}^{-2} \\ {x}_{2} & {x}_{1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
4+1+(-4)=1.

Consider the transformation f:R2→R2, defined as

f(x)=[x1+x2−1x1x2],x=[x1x2].

If the linear approximation of f at a=[212] is given by

f(x)≈[∗1]+[∗∗122](x−[212]),

what is the sum of the missing values?

a
112
b
1
c
9
d
52
e
54
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(x1+x2−1)=1,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(x1+x2−1)=−x2−2∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(x1x2)=x2,∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(x1x2)=x1

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[1−x2−2x2x1].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[212], we have

f(a)=[41],f′(a)=[1−4122].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[41]+[1−4122](x−[212]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

4+1+(−4)=1.

Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1} \\ {x}_{1}{x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}∗ & ∗ \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1})=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{-1})=-{x}_{2}^{-2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -{x}_{2}^{-2} \\ {x}_{2} & {x}_{1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & -4 \\ \frac{1}{2} & 2\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
4+1+(-4)=1.
$$

EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(x13−x22)=3x12,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(x13−x22)=−2x2∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(x1x2)=x2,∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(x1x2)=x1

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[3x12−2x2x2x1].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[−1−2], we have

f(a)=[−52],f′(a)=[34−2−1].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[−52]+[34−2−1](x−[−1−2]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

−5+4+(−2)=−3.

content.problem:
Consider the transformation $f:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2},$ defined as

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\ {x}_{1}{x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

If the linear approximation of $f$ at $a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]$ is given by 

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}∗ \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 & ∗ \\ ∗ & -1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]),
$$

what is the sum of the missing values?
content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2}^{2})=3{x}_{1}^{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{3}-{x}_{2}^{2})=-2{x}_{2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{2},\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}{x}_{2})={x}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{1}^{2} & -2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & {x}_{1}\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}3 & 4 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
-5+4+(-2)=-3.
$$

EXPLANATION

Suppose a transformation f:Rn→Rm is defined by

f:[x1x2⋮xn]⟶[f1(x1,x2,…,xn)f2(x1,x2,…,xn)⋮fm(x1,x2,…,xn)],

where f1,f2,…,fm are scalar functions with n variables. If f is differentiable at x, then the total derivative of f at x, denoted f′(x), is given by the m×n matrix

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2⋯∂f1∂xn∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2⋯∂f2∂xn⋮⋮⋮⋮∂fm∂x1∂fm∂x2⋯∂fm∂xn].

In our case, we have the following:

f′(x)=[∂f1∂x1∂f1∂x2∂f2∂x1∂f2∂x2]

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

∂f1∂x1=∂∂x1(x1+x22)=1,∂f1∂x2=∂∂x2(x1+x22)=2x2∂f2∂x1=∂∂x1(sin⁡(x1+x2))=cos⁡(x1+x2),∂f2∂x2=∂∂x2(sin⁡(x1+x2))=cos⁡(x1+x2)

Therefore, we have

f′(x)=[12x2cos⁡(x1+x2)cos⁡(x1+x2)].

Evaluating f and its derivative at x=a=[π2π2], we have

f(a)=[π2+π240],f′(a)=[1π−1−1].

The linear approximation of f at x=a is given by

f(x)≈f(a)+f′(a)(x−a).

Substituting f(a), f′(a), and a in the equation above, we obtain

f(x)≈[π2+π240]+[1π−1−1](x−[π2π2]).

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

0+π+(−1)=π−1.

content.worked_solution:
Suppose a transformation $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{m}$ is defined by 

$$
f:[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{f}_{1}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ {f}_{2}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}) \\ ⋮ \\ {f}_{m}({x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n})\end{aligned}],
$$

 

where ${f}_{1},{f}_{2},…,{f}_{m}$ are scalar functions with $n$ variables. If $f$ is differentiable at $x,$ then the total derivative of $f$ at $x,$ denoted ${f}^{′}(x),$ is given by the $m\times n$ matrix

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{n}} \\ ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ & ⋮ \\ \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂{f}_{m}}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}].
$$

In our case, we have the following:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}}\end{aligned}]
$$

First, we compute the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2})=1,\, & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}^{2})=2{x}_{2} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}))=\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}),\, & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & =\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}(\operatorname{sin}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}))=\operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2{x}_{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡({x}_{1}+{x}_{2})\end{aligned}].
$$

Evaluating $f$ and its derivative at $x=a=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
f(a)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{f}^{′}(a)=[\begin{aligned}1 & \pi  \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

The linear approximation of $f$ at $x=a$ is given by

$$
f(x)≈f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a).
$$

Substituting $f(a),$ ${f}^{′}(a),$ and $a$ in the equation above, we obtain

$$
f(x)≈[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & \pi  \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}](x-[\begin{aligned}\frac{\pi }{2} \\ \frac{\pi }{2}\end{aligned}]).
$$

Therefore, the sum of the missing values is

$$
0+\pi +(-1)=\pi -1.
$$
